title: Prepared Statements
learning_outcomes: Explain what prepared statements contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: preparing sql statements.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Database correctness depends on more than constructing a query. Use PDO prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, transactions for related changes, and bounded queries for predictable performance. In this lesson, focus on preparing sql statements; then compare it with binding parameters. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use prepared statements when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Database correctness depends on more than constructing a query. Use PDO prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, transactions for related changes, and bounded queries for predictable performance. For prepared statements, begin with preparing sql statements. Also distinguish binding parameters; executing statements; fetching results. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Preparing SQL statements
items.text: Keep query structure separate from data values, check failures explicitly, and use constraints or transactions when integrity depends on multiple operations.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Prepared Statements
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$sql = "SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE category = :category";
$params = [":category" => "books"];
echo str_contains($sql, ":category") && isset($params[":category"]) ? "named placeholder ready" : "check binding";

common_mistakes.why: Input can change the meaning of a query.
common_mistakes.fix: Use PDO prepared statements and bind values separately from the query text.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming application checks are enough for data integrity.
common_mistakes.why: Concurrent requests can race and bypass check-then-write assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Use unique constraints, foreign keys, transactions, and appropriate locking.

common_mistakes.why: Memory and response time can grow unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Use filtering and bounded pagination or streaming for large results.
